review.notes: Machine-drafted by an AI model; awaiting review by a Latinist. House style: simple Church Latin, spelled without macrons, with u/v and i/j as in Stage 0 (v and i only); present tense, with a few perfects (venit, vidit, fuit, dixit) in the last units.

english.source: drafted with the text; not reviewed

sentences.text: Anna in valetudinario est. Anna nutrix est. Hodie multi in valetudinario sunt.
sentences.english: Anna is at the clinic. Anna is a nurse. Today many people are at the clinic.

sentences.text: Martha quoque in valetudinario est. Martha non bene valet.
sentences.english: Martha is at the clinic too. Martha is not well.

sentences.text: Salve, Martha! Quomodo vales?
sentences.english: Hello, Martha! How are you?
sentences.speaker: ana

sentences.text: Non bene valeo, Anna. Caput meum dolet.
sentences.english: I am not well, Anna. My head hurts.
sentences.speaker: marta

sentences.text: Ubi dolet?
sentences.english: Where does it hurt?
sentences.speaker: ana

sentences.text: Hic. Et fessa sum.
sentences.english: Here. And I am tired.
sentences.speaker: marta

sentences.text: Quid habes? Quid vis?
sentences.english: What do you have? What do you want?
sentences.speaker: ana

sentences.text: Lac bibo, et panem edo. Aquam non bibo.
sentences.english: I drink milk, and I eat bread. I do not drink water.
sentences.speaker: marta

sentences.text: Aquam bibe! Aqua bona est.
sentences.english: Drink water! Water is good.
sentences.speaker: ana

sentences.text: Libenter aquam bibo. Et nunc?
sentences.english: I gladly drink water. And now?
sentences.speaker: marta

sentences.text: Hodie in domo manere bonum est.
sentences.english: Today it is good to stay at home.
sentences.speaker: ana

sentences.text: In domo maneo. Gratias tibi ago, Anna. Tu nutrix bona es.
sentences.english: I stay at home. Thank you, Anna. You are a good nurse.
sentences.speaker: marta

sentences.text: Vale, Martha! Pax tibi.
sentences.english: Goodbye, Martha! Peace to you.
sentences.speaker: ana

sentences.text: Martha domum it. Anna in valetudinario est.
sentences.english: Martha goes home. Anna is at the clinic.

sentences.text: Samuel quoque in valetudinario est. Samuel Annam videt.
sentences.english: Samuel is at the clinic too. Samuel sees Anna.

sentences.text: Salve, Anna! Manus mea dolet.
sentences.english: Hello, Anna! My hand hurts.
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: Ecce manus tua. Hic dolet?
sentences.english: Look, your hand. Does it hurt here?
sentences.speaker: ana

sentences.text: Ita, hic dolet!
sentences.english: Yes, it hurts here!
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: Manum in aqua habe. Aqua bona est.
sentences.english: Keep your hand in the water. The water is good.
sentences.speaker: ana

sentences.text: Manum in aqua habeo. Nunc manus non dolet.
sentences.english: I keep my hand in the water. Now my hand does not hurt.
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: Bene! Tu fessus es. Quid vis? Panem vis?
sentences.english: Good! You are tired. What do you want? Do you want bread?
sentences.speaker: ana

sentences.text: Panem volo, et aquam volo. Libenter edo, libenter bibo.
sentences.english: I want bread, and I want water. I gladly eat, I gladly drink.
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: Bene! Hodie in domo manere bonum est, Samuel. Cras in valetudinario es, sed non fessus.
sentences.english: Good! Today it is good to stay at home, Samuel. Tomorrow you are at the clinic, but not tired.
sentences.speaker: ana

sentences.text: Gratias tibi ago, Anna. Tu amica bona es!
sentences.english: Thank you, Anna. You are a good friend!
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: Anna in valetudinario laborat. Hodie Anna multum laborat. Lucius in schola laborat. Martha in domo non laborat.
sentences.english: Anna works at the clinic. Today Anna works a lot. Lucius works at school. Martha does not work at home.

sentences.text: Anna fessa est, sed bene valet. Omnes iuvat, et omnes Annam amant.
sentences.english: Anna is tired, but she is well. She helps everyone, and everyone loves Anna.

sentences.text: Lucius quoque in valetudinario est. Annam videt.
sentences.english: Lucius is at the clinic too. He sees Anna.

sentences.text: Salve, Anna! Quomodo vales? Fessane es?
sentences.english: Hello, Anna! How are you? Are you tired?
sentences.speaker: luis

sentences.text: Bene valeo, sed fessa sum. Quid habes, frater?
sentences.english: I am well, but I am tired. What do you have, brother?
sentences.speaker: ana

sentences.text: Ecce panis et lac. Tibi do. Tu soror bona es.
sentences.english: Look, bread and milk. I give them to you. You are a good sister.
sentences.speaker: luis

sentences.text: Gratias tibi ago, Luci! Tu frater bonus es. Hodie multum laboro, sed bene est.
sentences.english: Thank you, Lucius! You are a good brother. Today I work a lot, but it is well.
sentences.speaker: ana
